evidence.quote: In my view, while market volatility will continue to ebb and flow, these fluctuations are not likely to have important implications for policy.
The path of policy will depend on the progress of the economy toward fulfilment of the dual mandate.
Overall, accommodative monetary policy seems to have provided significant support for U.S. growth.
Taken together, developments in U.S. bond portfolios do not indicate a worrisome pickup in risk-taking in external investments.

We take the consequences of such spillovers seriously, and the Federal Reserve is intent on communicating its policy intentions as clearly as possible in order to reduce the likelihood of future disruptions to markets.

A slight hawkish tilt comes from saying market volatility will not sway policy as it returns to normal, but the net signal is essentially neutral.
